description: Livestream overlay drawn on the Jetson (A) against a clean JPEG plus per-frame data drawn by the browser (B). Benchmark replay, order A B B A, one fresh process per run, same frozen source copy, only a command-line flag differs.

input.format: 1280x720 H.264, replayed at 30 FPS; the pipeline runs at 1920x1080 and the livestream worker shrinks each frame to 1280x720

work_enabled: default profile with motion output off: pose detector, tracker with ReID, person lock, MediaPipe hands on the CPU (the default then), livestream at 20 FPS, 1080p recording. A Python client on the Jetson read /stream.mjpg?data=1 in both variants; no browser drew anything during timing.
window: 70-100 s after the viewer's first part, fixed before collection; perf averages from the worker every 2 s; /proc/stat and tegrastats every 1 s

metric_notes.worker_overlay_step_ms_mean: elapsed ms per livestream frame inside the encode worker, from its own timer. In this tree the timer starts before the 1080p->720p resize (area averaging), so both variants include the resize.
metric_notes.machine_cpu_busy_cores_proc_stat: busy CPU time / wall time over the window, whole machine, out of 6 cores; includes the Python viewer client and tegrastats.
metric_notes.main_process_cores: the stream's main process only; per-child CPU was not available in this capture.
metric_notes.tegrastats_window: 1 s tegrastats samples inside the window; tegrastats times are whole seconds and the monotonic-to-wall alignment is good to about 1 s. cpu_busy_x_clock_ghz = sum over cores of load x clock.

idle_microbenchmarks.note: idle board, sample counts not recorded

runs.variant: A: overlay drawn into the JPEG on the Jetson
B: clean JPEG + per-frame data, drawn by the browser
B: clean JPEG + per-frame data, drawn by the browser
